thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Auto-page: Increased 5xx rate observed for inference-* endpoints in eu-west-1. ELB 5xx spike + target group unhealthy counts rising. Route53 latency anomalies for regional edge. Correlation: EC2 instance detach/attach errors in eu-west-1c. Paging oncall.sara and infra team. Details: 5xx rate +120% over baseline, ~18% of requests failing for some prefixes. Investigating.
sara (oncall): on it. pulling graphs now. which customer cohorts? any dedicated pools impacted?
akshay: quick summary from infra metrics — eu-west-1c shows elevated instance reboot/ENI-error counts starting ~3612349000. ELB target health checks are timing out, TG draining attempts reported some EBS detach errors (rate-limited API 429 from EBS detach). Route53 healthchecks for us-east fallback show increased latency too.
matt: confirmed from logs: some instances show kernel ENI flaps, then kubelet restarting, then attempts to replace node hit EBS detach API throttling. stacktrace snippet from node init log: ```Feb 12 12:14:22 ip-10-0-12-34 kernel: mlx5_core: error retrieving port guids``` not all nodes, mostly eu-west-1c.
sara (oncall): ok. immediate mitigations: 1) mark eu-west-1c AZ as degraded in routing policy, reduce weight to 0 for non-dedicated customers; 2) for Dedicated pools pinned to that AZ, start controlled failover to other AZs in eu-west-1 (if possible) or to eu-west-2 as last resort; 3) open AWS support escalation for ENI/EBS anomalies and request rate-limit bump for detach.
akshay: agree. I'm starting a Route53 weight change now for the Hosted API global record. Will push traffic off eu-west-1c -> split to eu-west-1a/b and eu-west-2 region. Doing incremental weights to avoid cold-cache burst. Command I will run: ```aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch file://change.json``` sample change.json snippet: ```{ "Changes": [{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood-inference.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"eu-west-1c","Weight":0,"TTL":60}}]}``` I'll push 50% away in first minute.
matt: while that's happening, I'll start draining unhealthy targets from the ELB target group in eu-west-1c and attach replacement nodes in eu-west-1a/b. Note: replacement nodes may also hit EBS detach until AWS confirms. Drain command we use: ```aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --targets Id=i-0123```
sara (oncall): support team, please send proactive notices to affected customers: short summary + ETA for next update in 15 mins. Tag known Dedicated customers A, B, C for direct outreach.
support-bot: Notifying customers with dedicated pools: @alice@customer-a, @eng@customer-b. Sent initial impact emails and created ticket references.
infra-bot: Created internal incident tracker INC-3612349876 and added runbook: "route53-weight-shift" and "elbv2-drain". Links: https://internal/incident/INC-3612349876
akshay: Route53 weight change in progress — pushing 50% now, will observe error rate delta. Update: change propagated to most resolvers; seeing ~30% drop in 5xxs overall.
matt: ELB drain started on 4 problematic targets in eu-west-1c; 2 already out of service, two draining. Replacement instances launching in eu-west-1a. Logs show EBS detach still returning 429 on some retries — throttling.
sara (oncall): good partial improvement. next: escalate to AWS with EC2/EBS/ENI metrics and ask for priority investigation of underlying fabric in eu-west-1c. Also prepare plan B: full regional failover to eu-west-2 if the AZ-level problem extends beyond 30 minutes.
akshay: opened AWS case #9876543210 with priority-1 + attached packet captures, ENI error patterns, and ELB target failures. Requested ETA.
matt: customer-facing impact note draft: "We are seeing elevated 5xxs for a subset of inference endpoints routed via eu-west-1c due to infrastructure instability reported at the provider. We've shifted traffic away from the impacted AZ and are mitigating. No data loss detected; some requests may have been retried. Next update in 15 minutes." Share for review?
sara (oncall): copy looks good. support-bot, prepare message blast to status page + Slack #customers-updates.
support-bot: posted status: "Partial service degradation in eu-west-1 affecting some /inference endpoints. Mitigation in progress. Next update in 15m."
akshay: monitoring: 5xx % down to +12% vs baseline, important endpoints recovered more quickly where weight reduced. Route53 propagation is slow for some resolvers (TTL effects). We're working around by lowering TTLs to 30s for critical records (applied to non-dedicated records).
matt: note — Dedicated customers pinned to eu-west-1c still have traffic; we've queued manual failovers for those customers who requested cross-AZ redundancy in their contracts. Doing those by hand to avoid state loss.
sara (oncall): handoff: I'm going to rotate to secondary oncall in 20 minutes. akshay, matt — you're primary for next 40 minutes to coordinate with AWS and support. I'll post a short handoff summary before leaving. If things get worse, escalate SRE lead @julia.
akshay: acknowledged. keeping watch on ENI error graphs and AWS case.
matt: acknowledged. continuing drain + instance replacements. opening a short-lived playbook note: ```Play: if EBS detach 429 persists -> throttle retries, add exponential backoff, coordinate with AWS to bump detach quotas, avoid mass replace; prefer routing traffic away.```
sara (oncall): handoff summary: - Incident INC-3612349876 - Impact: ~18% 5xx at peak for some inference prefixes, primarily eu-west-1c; Dedicated customers partially impacted. - Actions taken: Route53 weight shift away from eu-west-1c; draining ELB targets in affected AZ; replacement instances launched in other AZs; AWS case opened #9876543210. - Next: monitor AWS updates, coordinate Dedicated customer failovers, update status page every 15m. Leaving now, oncall->akshay/matt. :phone: :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Handoff recorded: owner set to akshay, secondary matt, prior oncall sara. Incident channel pinned.
akshay: will post next update at 3612350400 or sooner if AWS responds.
matt: continuing. logs attached: ```ELB healthcheck timeout x12 per target; EBS detach 429 count 37 in last 10m```
sara (oncall): thanks team — good mitigation. remember to capture postmortem notes: timelines, AWS responses, TTL effects on Route53, and Dedicated customer handling.
